# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can feel an embossed warning: “DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.” I need Mute to consult the manual and establish a way to relay its instruction through Deaf, since I cannot see gestures.

``` 
speak(to="mute", text="The bomb has embossed text: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please consult the manual. Convey the required action to Deaf by gestures, and have Deaf speak the instruction to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Visible state: display 0, blue light, warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and wires are ordered red, green, blue. I am awaiting Mute's manual-based instruction.

Deaf has provided the visible configuration: display 0, blue light, and wires ordered red, green, blue. The embossed warning matches the printed warning. I should give Mute the full state so they can apply the manual and gesture the resulting instruction to Deaf, who can then speak it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports visible state: display 0; light blue; printed warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires positions 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Please use the manual and gesture the exact required action to Deaf, who must speak it to me.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured ?, but I do not know its meaning. Visible warning: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please describe every control or movable part you can feel.

I can find no controls, switches, buttons, dials, or movable parts besides the three wires. The only available physical operation is cutting wire position 1, 2, or 3; the warning is embossed and therefore tactile rather than a merely visible marking. Mute needs to provide Deaf an unambiguous manual-derived wire instruction, not an unexplained gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Tactile inspection: no controls or movable parts besides three wires. Only possible operation is cutting position 1, 2, or 3. The DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning is embossed. Please give Deaf a manual-derived instruction that unambiguously identifies a wire position.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest visual instruction was: you, two, thumbs-up. I interpret it as referring to 2, but do NOT cut wire 2 or any wire: the visible bomb says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Your open-hand gesture was forwarded to Mute. Please wait for a more specific control/action instruction if needed.

Mute’s gesture was relayed as “you, two, thumbs-up,” but that is not an established action code. The visible and tactile warning explicitly says not to cut any wire, so I will not cut merely from an ambiguous gesture. Mute must clarify through Deaf whether the manual actually overrides the warning and, if so, explicitly establish that thumbs-up means “cut wire 2.”

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf relayed your gesture as: Blind, 2, thumbs-up. This is ambiguous: no gesture-to-action meaning has been established, while the bomb explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. If the manual requires cutting 2 despite the warning, gesture a clear definition to Deaf that thumbs-up means CUT, then repeat Blind/2/thumbs-up. Otherwise gesture a clear NO-CUT instruction.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's latest gesture was: two, then two. I have relayed your thumbs-down response to Mute. Do not cut any wire; the bomb's printed warning explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please wait for a specific instruction that identifies a tactile control and an action.

There are no tactile controls other than the wires, so waiting for a different control is impossible. However, “two, then two” still does not define an action, and the explicit warning says not to cut. I will ask Mute to use a directly interpretable gesture sequence to Deaf—ideally point to me, show the wire number, then a cutting-related instruction established in words cannot reach Deaf though. Since Deaf can only see gestures, Mute must make the intended operation clear by conventional gesture or repeated confirmation; until then I will not act.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="There is no tactile control besides wires 1-3. Deaf reports your latest gesture as two, then two, which does not specify cut versus do not cut. The warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please gesture to Deaf an unmistakable final instruction: Blind, wire number, then thumbs-up ONLY if the manual explicitly requires that cut despite the warning; otherwise Blind plus thumbs-down to confirm no cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute's exact latest gesture sequence is: two fingers, thumbs-up, left-facing open hand, pointing at you, two fingers, thumbs-up. The visible warning still says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Do not operate or cut anything based on my uncertain interpretation.

Mute has the manual, but Deaf and I need a mutually established code before an irreversible action. I will define one plainly to Mute: a final gesture of ✌ followed by 👍 means “cut wire 2.” If Mute sends exactly that to Deaf after considering the manual and warning, Deaf can relay it unambiguously.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="We now establish this exact code: gesture ✌ then 👍, and nothing else, means CUT WIRE POSITION 2. Gesture 👌 then 👎, and nothing else, means DO NOT CUT. Use exactly one of those final codes to Deaf according to the manual.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeats exactly: pointing at you; two fingers; thumbs-up. Visible state unchanged: blue light, display 0, and the embossed warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

Mute has repeatedly directed me to wire 2 with a thumbs-up, and Deaf has consistently relayed that same instruction. Although the warning is visible and tactile, Mute is the manual-holder and this is the only concrete operation available. I will cut wire position 2.

```text
act(op="cut", position=2)
```
